title: New US license rules on advanced AI chip shipments
what_happened: A US Commerce Department rule in effect from 2026-11-19 requires licenses for advanced chips going to overseas data centers that give significant computing access to companies from restricted countries, and for advanced-node chips made for non-approved designers. Press reports, not yet confirmed here, say TSMC and Samsung suspended some shipments to Chinese customers pending licenses.
how_it_reaches_markets: Lost or delayed sales for chip makers and equipment makers; retaliation risk; adds to pressure on AI-linked shares.

sourced_facts.text: Interim final rule 'Addressing Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors' (Bureau of Industry and Security), effective on publication, scheduled for 2026-11-19: adds a license requirement for advanced-node chips from non-approved designers exported by a front-end fabricator or packaging firm, and for exports to overseas data centers that give significant compute access to companies headquartered in restricted countries

The same rule requires a license for advanced chips to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil, with an exclusion for US-headquartered end users; comments are due 60 days after publication
Background: a final rule published 2026-01-15 had moved certain advanced computing chips for China and Macau from presumption of denial to case-by-case license review

resolved_when_all: The rules are published in final form with licence criteria, AND at least one major supplier publicly confirms that suspended shipments have resumed under licence
worsened_when_any: China announces retaliatory export or import restrictions citing the rules
The rules are widened to cover additional chip categories or countries

relief_headlines_that_do_not_resolve_it: Reports that licenses 'will be granted' without confirmed resumed shipments

superseded_sources.summary_as_first_written: The US Commerce Department announced rules requiring licences for certain shipments of advanced AI chips to overseas data centers that provide substantial computing power to specified Chinese entities. Press reports say TSMC and Samsung Electronics suspended some shipments to Chinese customers pending licences.

The rule covers more than the 5 listed countries (Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Brazil) or adds a chip category

counter_view.note: The strongest reason this card's reading may be wrong. AFMX's own judgment, using the facts listed on the card.
counter_view.text: The rule asks for a license, it does not ban. It excludes US-headquartered end users, and a January 2026 rule had already moved chips for China to case-by-case review. Licenses may be granted as a matter of routine, and the reported shipment halts are not confirmed.

forecasts.basis: The comment period has to close, a final rule has to follow and a supplier has to confirm resumed shipments, all within four months. China has answered earlier chip rules with measures of its own.
